financial_ontology._note: General financial/accounting term definitions — standard knowledge, NOT disclosed by or specific to this RHP. No source_page: these are not RHP citations. Distinct from glossary_sample, which holds terms the RHP itself defines with page references. Narration rules for this section (see 05_query_engine.py ONTOLOGY_ADDENDUM) forbid inventing a page citation for these.

terms.definition: A profitability ratio measuring how efficiently a company generates profit from shareholders' equity. Calculated as Net Profit / Net Worth, expressed as a percentage.
A company's net worth (total assets minus total liabilities) divided by its total number of outstanding equity shares.

Net profit attributable to equity shareholders divided by the number of equity shares. 'Basic EPS' uses the actual weighted-average share count; 'Diluted EPS' assumes conversion of instruments like CCPS into equity shares, which lowers the per-share figure.
Share price divided by earnings per share. Indicates how much investors are paying per unit of the company's earnings; a common (though not sole) valuation comparison metric between peer companies.

Total borrowings divided by total shareholders' equity. Indicates how much of the company's financing comes from debt relative to owners' capital; a higher ratio generally means greater reliance on borrowed funds.
The annualized average growth rate of a value over a specified period longer than one year, assuming growth compounds each year. Smooths out year-to-year volatility into a single average rate.

A general accounting/disclosure principle: information is 'material' if its omission or misstatement could reasonably influence the decisions of someone relying on it. Companies typically set their own numeric materiality thresholds (e.g. a percentage of profit or net worth) to decide what must be individually disclosed versus what can be aggregated.
